summary: Georeferenced radiolarian occurrences are open at scale: OBIS holds 724,395 records (512 taxa in its checklist) and PBDB 13,020 fossil occurrences (103 dated to the Cambrian interval), and the Neptune database is archived on Zenodo (CC BY, PostgreSQL/SQLite dumps). That covers range, local richness and stratigraphic-span variables in principle, but sample-level tables, taxonomic validation and sampling-effort controls were not checked, and Cambrian-to-Recent identity of families needs taxonomic work that none of the sources supplies.
next_step: Download the Neptune SQLite and an OBIS radiolarian extract in a separate step, filter to valid species, and pre-register range-size, local-richness and dominance metrics with a sampling-effort control before testing.
obstacles_confirmed: Sampling effort and synonymy are uncontrolled in raw occurrence tables.
Neptune is Cenozoic-weighted by design; Palaeozoic radiolarian coverage rests on PBDB's 13,020 records.
